title: Input and Output
goal: printf/scanf family, format specifiers, string input aur input validation ko safely use karna.
definition: C me standard I/O streams (stdin, stdout, stderr) ke through hota hai. printf formatted output deta hai; scanf formatted input padhta hai; getchar/putchar characters; fgets line-based safe string input deta hai.
explain: printf format string + arguments leta hai. Har % specifier batata hai value kaise print karni hai: %d int, %f double, %c char, %s string, %p pointer, %zu size_t.
scanf ko address chahiye, value nahi — isliye & lagta hai: scanf("%d", &age). String (char array) me & ki zaroorat nahi kyunki array khud address me decay hota hai.
scanf whitespace par rukta hai, isliye spaces wala naam %s se poora nahi padha jaata. Line padhne ke liye fgets(buffer, size, stdin) use karo — buffer overflow se bachne ka safe rasta.
Mixed scanf aur fgets me leftover newline bug aata hai: scanf ke baad buffer me \n bacha rehta hai. getchar() se consume karo ya poora line-based input lo.
Production input par kabhi bharosa mat karo: return value check karo (scanf kitne items padhe), range validate karo, aur fgets ke baad newline trim karo.
analogy: printf ek printer hai jo format template ke hisaab se values bharta hai. scanf ek form hai jisme aapko batane padta hai value kahan likhni hai — isliye address (&) dena padta hai, warna form kahin aur bhar jaayega (crash).
why: User input hi real programs ka pehla attack surface hai. Galat format specifier UB deta hai, unbounded %s buffer overflow — security bug. Sahi I/O likhna aage ke saare interactive programs ki neenv hai.

syntax.note: printf me double ke liye %f (ya %lf, same), scanf me double ke liye %lf zaroori.
Return value check karo; fgets newline chhodta hai, trim karo.
Left/right align, zero pad, sign, hex — width aur flags.

topics.title: Format specifiers
topics.body: %d/%i signed int, %u unsigned, %f double (printf), %lf scanf double, %c char, %s string, %ld long, %lld long long, %x hex, %o octal, %p pointer, %zu size_t, %% literal percent. Specifier aur argument type mismatch UB hai.

topics.title: Width, precision, flags
topics.body: %8d width 8 right align; %-8d left; %08d zero pad; %.3f 3 decimals; %+d force sign; %#x 0x prefix. Width runtime se bhi de sakte ho: printf("%*d", 5, x).

topics.title: scanf aur validation
topics.body: scanf address leta hai, whitespace skip karta hai, return value me successful conversions deta hai. Failure par input stream me galat characters bache rehte hain — unhe consume karo warna infinite loop. %s me width do: %31s.

topics.title: Character aur line input
topics.body: getchar/putchar int return karte hain taaki EOF (-1) represent ho. fgets newline include karta hai aur buffer size se zyada nahi padhta — isliye safe. puts newline add karta hai; fputs nahi.

topics.title: Buffers aur streams
topics.body: stdout line-buffered (terminal) ya fully buffered (file) ho sakta hai; program crash par buffer ka data kho sakta hai. Debug me fflush(stdout) ya stderr use karo. stderr unbuffered hai. Input buffer me leftover newline sabse common beginner bug hai.

mistakes.why: scanf address maangta hai; value dene par crash/UB.
Bina width ke overflow ho sakta hai; fgets behtar hai.
scanf me double ke liye %lf; %f float ke liye.

debug.brief: scanf ke baad fgets turant khali line padh raha hai. Bug fix karo.
hints: Ek getchar() se leftover newline consume karo.
debug.fix: scanf("%d", &n); getchar(); fgets(line, sizeof line, stdin);

best: scanf ka return value check karo
String input ke liye fgets + newline trim
printf format aur argument type match karo
User input ko range validate karo
Prompt ke baad fflush(stdout) debug me

mcqs.q: scanf me double ke liye kaunsa specifier?
mcqs.explain: scanf me %lf; printf me %f ya %lf dono double ke liye chalte hain (default promotion).

mcqs.q: fgets newline ke saath kya karta hai?
mcqs.explain: fgets newline include karta hai agar jagah ho; trim karna padta hai.
int, taaki EOF (-1) char se alag represent ho.

interview.q: scanf aur fgets me kya safe hai?
interview.a: fgets buffer size leta hai, isliye overflow nahi hota; scanf %s unbounded hai jab tak width na do (%31s). Line input ke liye fgets better hai.
interview.followUp: fgets newline? — include karta hai, trim karo.

interview.a: Undefined behaviour: galat bytes padhe jaate hain, garbage ya crash. Compiler -Wformat warning deta hai.
interview.followUp: printf("%d", 3.5) kyun galat? — double varargs me double hi jaata hai, %d int expect karta hai.

interview.a: stdout buffered hai (line ya full), stderr unbuffered — errors turant dikhte hain aur redirection se alag file me ja sakte hain.
